name: Kyushu, Japan
summary: Volcanoes, a rural hot-spring valley, a restored castle town and a harbour city, tied together without the Kyoto blossom crush. Best if you travel after 8 April and leave before 29 April 2027.
why: The children get trains, food, myths and a real landscape. The adults get design, history and onsen towns. A group of seven is easier on trains and one rental car than in a string of European hire vans. Mid-April is the quiet part of Kyushu's spring.
distinctive: A giant caldera, a gorge tied to founding myths, and Nagasaki's layered history, in a part of Japan that most first trips skip.
weather: A family guide to Kyushu cites Fukuoka around 20°C by day and 12°C at night in April. That matches the usual spring pattern: mild, sometimes wet, good for walking. Confirm the year with the Japan Meteorological Agency.
crowds: Kyushu lowland cherries often peak in late March or the first days of April. In 2026, full bloom was recorded in the first week of April in Fukuoka, Kumamoto, Nagasaki and nearby cities. The first week also catches the end of Japanese spring break. Golden Week 2027 starts on Thursday 29 April. The useful gap is about 8–25 April.
natureExperiences: Mount Aso's grasslands, if volcanic-gas levels allow
Takachiho Gorge and its myth caves, as a long day rather than a new country
Beppu's steaming vents, from the paths only
age6: Trains, castle grounds, a river or seaside promenade, and a private family bath. Public mixed onsen is not the plan.
age12: The Aso caldera, Takachiho's story, castle museums, and choosing the day's noodles.
age14: Nagasaki's history, in the dose they can handle, plus the rail network itself. This is the destination where the 14-year-old has the most to do.
adults: Food, design, onsen etiquette, and two serious histories: a castle town and an international port. Kyoto is not required.
gettingAround: Trains between the cities. One rental car for the Aso and Takachiho days, because rural buses will exhaust a group of seven. Japan drives on the left, like both families. An International Driving Permit is worth confirming with the rental company rather than assuming.
meetingPoint: Fukuoka (Hakata). Bengaluru and Melbourne both normally connect, often via Seoul, Singapore, Hong Kong or Tokyo. Do not treat a direct Fukuoka flight from either city as real until the 2027 schedule shows it.
visaAu: Australian passports do not need a visa for a short tourist stay of up to 90 days. Japan's Ministry of Foreign Affairs lists Australia among the visa-exempt nationalities.
visaIn: Indian passports are not on Japan's visa-exempt list. The Consulate-General of Japan in Bengaluru, through VFS, accepts tourist applications from people who currently live in Karnataka. A passport issued outside Karnataka needs Karnataka residence proof. The published checklist asks for the Bangalore flights and says a family travelling together from Bangalore should lodge together. The consulate's stated time is a minimum of six working days, and that is only a guide. If the four travellers do not live in Karnataka, use the consulate for their home, not the departure airport.
disadvantages: The first week of April and anything from 29 April onward are the wrong weeks.
Takachiho is a long drive. It is the one demanding transfer in an otherwise gentle route.
Public baths are often not set up for a mixed-age family. Book a room with a private bath.
Cherry blossom is mostly over in the cities by mid-April. Come for green hills and late flowers, not a hanami festival.
uncertainties: Whether Aso is open to visitors that week. Gas levels close the crater rim without much notice.
International seats out of Nagasaki. If they are poor, spend the last night back in Fukuoka.

gain: The best shared trip for the 12- and 14-year-olds, with trains doing the hard logistics.
miss: Wild empty nature on the scale of Fiordland or Jiuzhaigou, and a visa-free path for Indian passports.

cost.summary: Melbourne fares about ₹1.8–2.3 lakh for three adults. Bengaluru fares about ₹1.6–5.3 lakh for four adults, because the published airline bands are far apart. Visa fees about ₹5,200. Hotels and food are not included.

lines.text: Kayak.com.au’s typical return fare, Melbourne to Fukuoka, was A$920–$1,148 for one adult. Three adult fares are about ₹1.8–2.3 lakh at ₹66.47 per Australian dollar. One stop. Not an April 2027 quote.

A Google Flights route page showed past-year typical return fares of about US$425–$710 on one airline and about US$700–$1,400 on another. Four adult fares across that spread are about ₹1.6–5.3 lakh at ₹94.86 per US dollar. Not an April 2027 quote.

Australian passports pay no visa fee for a short stay. The Bengaluru visa centre listed an Indian single-entry fee of ₹500 plus a service charge of ₹800, about ₹1,300 an application, or about ₹5,200 for four. The list does not show a different child fee. Optional courier was extra.

cost.leftOut: Hotels, meals, trains, the rental car and tickets are not included.

trip.note: Flights from both cities and the Japan visa fee are inside this.
trip.text: A band for seven people and about 13 nights, rounded to the nearest lakh. Not a quote, and not used to order the list. Three rooms, meals for seven, local transport and tickets. The 6-year-old's meals are not discounted. Insurance, bags and shopping are outside it. Meals, local transport and tickets use Japan-wide Budget Your Trip figures from 5 September 2026, not a Fukuoka-only table. The low end uses that site's budget stay. The high end uses a published Fukuoka April room price of about US$181 for each of three rooms, plus the mid-range meals and tickets.

stretch16: Add a free day in Yufuin and a free day in Fukuoka. Do not add Tokyo.

days.experience: Arrive and walk Ohori Park or the canal if the timing is kind.
days.optional: A department-store meal, which solves the first dinner
days.highlight: A compact city that is easy after a long flight
days.kids: Park first. No sightseeing list today.
days.transfer: Both families aim for Fukuoka Airport or Hakata. Confirm 2027 connections.
days.seasonal: Do not land into the 29 April holiday if you can choose.
days.wet: Canal City and an early night.

days.experience: Castle ruins, Maizuru Park, and the Momochi seaside.
days.optional: Fukuoka Tower only if the children ask
days.highlight: A city beach and a castle ground in one afternoon
days.kids: Space to run, then food they can point at.
days.transfer: Subway and short taxis. No car yet.
days.seasonal: City cherries are usually finished by the second week of April.
days.wet: A covered shopping street and a science or children's museum if one is open nearby.

days.experience: Dazaifu shrine and the approach street.
days.optional: Kyushu National Museum if the 12- and 14-year-olds want the indoor hour
days.highlight: A shrine town that feels like a story, close to the city
days.kids: The 6-year-old gets the street and the grounds. The museum is optional for the older two.
days.transfer: About half an hour by train from Fukuoka. Confirm the line on the day.
days.wet: The museum becomes the main event.

days.experience: Itoshima coast. A slow day of sea, bakeries and a short walk.
days.highlight: A quieter shoreline west of the city
days.kids: The sea will be cool. This is looking and paddling at the edge, not a swim holiday.
days.transfer: Train or a hired car for the day. Roughly under an hour.
days.wet: Stay in Fukuoka and repeat a favourite meal.

days.experience: Limited express into the hot-spring valley. Walk the town once and stop.
days.highlight: A small valley town built around steam and guesthouses
days.transfer: Hakata to Yufuin is about 2 hours by limited express. Confirm the JR Kyushu 2027 time.
days.seasonal: Book the room with a private bath. Do not rely on a public mixed bath.

days.experience: A floral park or a lakeside loop, then nothing else.
days.optional: Rent cycles if the 6-year-old has a seat option
days.kids: All three can do a short loop. End before anyone is bored.
days.transfer: On foot from the station area.
days.seasonal: Mid-April is green and floral rather than peak cherry.
days.wet: Craft shops and the private bath.

days.experience: Beppu's hells: viewing paths around steaming vents.
days.optional: A foot bath, not a swim in a volcanic pool
days.highlight: The ground itself is hot. Stay on the marked paths.
days.kids: Hold the 6-year-old's hand. The drama is real and so is the risk if anyone climbs a fence.
days.transfer: About an hour from Yufuin. A local bus or taxi loop is enough.
days.seasonal: Steam is year-round. Rain makes paths slippery.
days.wet: Go anyway with shoes that grip, or skip it and keep the valley day.

days.experience: Pick up a car and drive to a base near Aso, not a new city every night.
days.optional: One easy grassland stop if you arrive early
days.highlight: The scale of the caldera as you drop into it
days.kids: Car day. Snacks and a clear stop.
days.transfer: Allow about 2.5–3.5 hours depending on the exact base. This is an estimate.
days.seasonal: Rural Japan is the reason for the car. Return it in Kumamoto before Nagasaki.
days.wet: Drive to the hotel and use the indoor onsen plan.

days.experience: Aso caldera and Kusasenri meadow, if the gas report is safe.
days.optional: A short horse-riding loop only with an operator who takes age 6
days.kids: Meadows suit all three. The crater rim is a decision on the morning.
days.seasonal: The Japan Meteorological Agency and the local Aso page decide closures. Have Kumamoto city ready as the backup.
days.wet: Kumamoto Castle and Suizenji Garden a day early.

days.optional: The castle reconstruction story for the 14-year-old
days.highlight: A castle rebuilt after the 2016 earthquakes, and a garden modelled on famous landscapes
days.kids: Grounds for the 6-year-old. Museums for the older two.
days.transfer: Under an hour from an Aso base to the city, depending where you slept.
days.seasonal: Castle hours change. Check the morning of the visit.

days.experience: Takachiho Gorge. Go early, row the gorge boat if it is running, see one shrine, drive back.
days.optional: Amano Iwato shrine, told as a story rather than a long temple tour
days.highlight: A narrow gorge and the myth of the sun goddess
days.kids: The boat and the story work for all three. The day is long because of the drive, not the walk.
days.transfer: Roughly 2.5–3 hours each way from the Aso–Kumamoto area. Confirm the route. Drop this day on a 10- or 12-day trip.
days.seasonal: Boat operations stop in high water or wind.
days.wet: If the gorge is raining heavily, keep the castle day and do not add a slippery gorge.

days.experience: A free day in the countryside or a second pass at a favourite Aso viewpoint.
days.highlight: Space after the long gorge day
days.transfer: None if you skip the car.
days.seasonal: Use this day first if Aso was closed earlier.

days.experience: Train to Nagasaki. Glover Garden and the harbour slopes.
days.optional: A tram ride, which is enough adventure by itself
days.highlight: A steep port city with a foreign-trading past
days.kids: Glover Garden is the right scale for age 6. Use the slope car or tram rather than forcing every stair.
days.transfer: Return the car in Kumamoto. Kumamoto to Nagasaki is often about 2–3 hours with a change. Confirm JR or highway bus.
days.seasonal: Neighbourhood slopes are always stairs. The tram is the kindness.
days.wet: Glover Garden's indoor houses and a covered market.

days.experience: Peace Park in the morning for the older children. A harbour hour for the 6-year-old.
days.optional: The atomic-bomb museum only if the 12- and 14-year-olds want it, with a parent who can leave
days.highlight: A serious place, taken in a small dose
days.kids: Do not walk the 6-year-old through the full museum. The park and the paper cranes are enough at that age.
days.transfer: If the flight home is from Fukuoka, allow about 2 hours back by train and do not sightsee that morning. Confirm which airport has seven seats.
days.seasonal: This day is emotional, not seasonal. Keep it short.
days.wet: The museum is indoors. Still keep the visit short.
